newsitem.title: USA: US Treasuries open a bit higher before Q3 GDP data.
newsitem.headline: US Treasuries open a bit higher before Q3 GDP data.

text.p: U.S. Treasury prices opened slightly higher on Wednesday in front of the goverment's release of third-quarter GDP data with analysts saying that the market could build on Tuesday's spectacular rally.

"The outlook is positive," said Patrick Dimick, Treasury market analyst at CS First Boston. "There was broad-based buying overnight all across the yield curve from Asian accounts during the London session.
The 6-3/4 percent 30-year bond was unchanged at 100-27/32, yielding 6.68 percent in early trade.
Dimick said panic-buying fueled the market's march higher.

"There's substantial panic-buying by any money managers holding on to cash," he said. "They can't afford to be left behind in this rally. They're fearful that yesterday's 15-basis-point move (on the 30-year bond yield) is only one part of a total 30- to 40-basis-point move. They're buying in fear that this is going to be a huge breakout move. That's what we saw overnight and that portends very bullishly for our market."
At 0830 EST/1330 GMT, the government will issue its first estimate of third-quarter Gross Domestic Product (GDP).
Economists surveyed by Reuters estimated, on average, that GDP grew 1.8 percent in the quarter, a substantial slowing from the 4.7 percent rate in the second quarter.
Dimick said if the "final sales" aspect of GDP is 0.7 percent, U.S. portfolio managers will also buy the market aggressively.

Another piece of economic data likely to favor the bond market is the Commerce Department's report on single-family home sales in September. Set for release at 1000 EST/1500 GMT, home sales are believed to have occured at an annualized rate of 768,000 in September, down from 832,000 in November.

Any gains the market scores today will come on top of a powerful rally on Tuesday inspired by news that wage costs grew a moderate 0.6 percent in the third quarter, less than the market had anticipated.
Economists said the data showed that labor market tightness was not translating into higher wages.

That news, supplemented by a drop in the Conference Board's measure of October consumer confidence, made a Federal Reserve interest-rate hike this calendar year pretty well erased any residual fears of a Federal Reserve interest-rate hike this calendar year, economists said.

The market also gets the Federal Reserve's Beige Book at 1200 EST/1700 GMT. The Beige Book is a periodic, anecdotal account of business conditions around the nation. Economists expect it to reflect what recent data have indicated -- that economic growth is moderating and that wage pressures are scattered, at most.
In early trade, the 6-3/4 percent 30-year bond edged up 2/32 to 100-29/32, yielding 6.68 percent.
Three-month rates were unchanged at 5.01 percent, six-month rates down one basis point to 5.07 percent and year-bill rates down two basis points to 5.14 percent.
Two-year notes were up 1/32 to 100-8/32, yielding 5.74 percent. Five-year notes were up 2/32 to 100-21/32, yielding 6.10 percent.
The 6-1/2 percent ten-year note was up 3/32 to 100-29/32 to 6.38 percent.
